text:
carmen: Heads up — I merged the alloc-scheduler tweak (PR 8971) into canary earlier. Canary bench shows a p95 memory jump (~1.8G -> 2.2G) and two OOMs in the last hour. attaching bench: https://bench.internal/runs/175500

todd: ack. can you drop the raw numbers and any logs? p95/mem before vs after?

carmen: pre-merge p95=1.8G, post-merge p95=2.2G, throughput ~flat, tail latency unchanged. OOMs hit at 2.5G heap. logs: https://logs.internal/alloc/175500 (contains stack traces)

sree: not great. does the change increase in-flight buffers or delay frees? any quick heap profiles?

carmen: initial heap profile points at retained allocations in slicePool and delayed free paths for KV-shard entries. flamegraph: https://graphs.internal/flames/175500

jordan: ran a short local profile: `tools/profiler -m 30s --target alloc-svc --tag canary` — shows large retained slices from `slicePool.get()`, plus increased GC pause cumulatives.

todd: can we revert the canary to pre-merge and re-run the bench before we approve anything further? if it's correlated we should rollback fast.

carmen: rolling back canary now. will post quick numbers in ~10m.

bench-bot: bench run started (id: 175500-rollback-check). comparison id: cmp-8892. I'll post a summary when finished.

ops-oncall: noted the OOMs — I bumped pod memory limits on canary and increased retry budget to avoid user-facing errors while you investigate.

carmen: rollback applied. quick smoke: p95 back to ~1.79G, no OOMs in first 8m. scheduling a full bench run.

sree: once full bench completes let's collect: 1) flamegraphs pre/post, 2) heap histograms, 3) alloc traces for slicePool. then open a follow-up PR to tighten buffer sizing or change pool behavior. cc @jordan for review.

todd: sounds good. if bench confirms, I'll approve the rollback PR and we can queue a conservative scheduler rework (smaller incremental changes). :thumbsup:

carmen: interim summary: merged tweak -> +22% p95 memory and 2 OOMs; rollback -> baseline restored. Next: open PR to adjust slicePool sizing + add mem regression test in microbench harness. links: bench summary: https://bench.internal/runs/175500 cmp:cmp-8892 flame: https://graphs.internal/flames/175500 logs: https://logs.internal/alloc/175500

jordan: I'll add a regression test to the microbench harness to assert max-resident < 2.0G for the long-seq workload and add the flamegraph artifacts to the CI job.

carmen: thanks everyone. I'll open the follow-up PR and tag reviewers, and include the bench artifacts. :eyes:
